title: Introduction to integers
competency: Use integers for temperature, altitude and money; define the set of integers and show integers on a number line.

keywords.def: A number below zero, written with a minus sign, like −5.
A number above zero, like +5 or 5.
A whole number or the negative of a whole number. ℤ = {…, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, …}.
A line with 0 in the middle, positives to the right and negatives to the left.
Two numbers at the same distance from 0 on different sides, like 4 and −4.

en.text: Temperatures below zero get a minus sign, like minus 5 degrees. These are negative numbers. Numbers above zero are positive, like plus 15. We use the same signs for loss and profit, or below and above sea level.

screens.title: Cold morning
screens.ask: On Tuesday, Debre Birhan was 5 °C below zero. How can we write it?
screens.after:
Below zero gets a minus sign: −5 °C.
Above zero gets a plus sign, or no sign: +5 °C or 5 °C.
So 5 °C and +5 °C both mean above zero. They are wrong here.

screens.title: 2.2 Introduction to integers
paras: Anders Celsius (1701–1744) found a way to measure temperature.
Debre Birhan had 15 °C above zero, then 5 °C and 10 °C below zero.

screens.title: Debre Birhan temperatures

points.label: Wed −10 °C
points.info: 10 steps left of 0: the coldest day.

screens.ask: Tap each day. Which side of 0 is it on?

screens.title: Note
paras: Temperatures below zero use a minus sign. They are negative numbers.
Temperatures above zero use a plus sign. They are positive numbers.
A positive number can be written without the plus sign: +2 is 2.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A number below zero, written with a minus sign, like −5.
A number above zero, like +5 or 5.

screens.text: Write the temperature with a sign: 6 °C below zero is written
screens.why:
Below zero means less than 0.
Numbers less than 0 get a minus sign.
So 6 °C below zero is −6 °C.
+6 °C and 6 °C mean 6 °C above zero.

screens.ask: Write the money with a sign: a loss of Birr 100 is written ___
screens.why:
A gain makes your money go up: plus sign.
A loss makes your money go down: minus sign.
So a loss of Birr 100 is −100.
screens.clue: Is a loss a gain or a decrease?

screens.title: Positive or negative? Sort each quantity.
screens.why:
Rise, forward, above zero and gain are positive.
A rise of 10 °C = +10. 7 km forward = +7. 21 °C above zero = +21.
Below zero and loss are negative.
6 °C below zero = −6. A loss of Birr 100 = −100.
screens.clue: Is it more than zero or less than zero?

screens.text: Compare temperatures: which day was the coldest? Monday +15 °C, Tuesday −5 °C or Wednesday −10 °C?
screens.why:
The coldest day has the lowest temperature.
+15 °C is above zero, so Monday is warm.
−5 °C is 5 below zero. −10 °C is 10 below zero.
10 below zero is colder than 5 below zero.
So Wednesday (−10 °C) was the coldest.

screens.ask: Heights as integers: Ras Dashen is 4550 m above sea level. The Danakil Depression is 125 m below sea level. Write the Danakil height as an integer: ___ m
screens.why:
Sea level works like zero.
Above sea level is positive: Ras Dashen is +4550 m.
Below sea level is negative.
So the Danakil Depression is −125 m.

en.text: Integers are the whole numbers together with the negative numbers. ℤ is the set of integers. Zero is an integer that is neither positive nor negative. Fractions and decimals like 2.5 are not integers. Natural numbers sit inside whole numbers, which sit inside the integers.

screens.title: Integer or not?
screens.after:
2.5 = 2 + 0.5. It has a decimal part.
Integers are …, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, … with no fraction or decimal part.
2.5 lies between 2 and 3, so it is not an integer.

screens.title: Definition 2.3
paras: An integer is a whole number or a negative number.

screens.title: ℕ ⊂ 𝕎 ⊂ ℤ
screens.ask: Tap a circle, then each number.
numbers: A negative integer: only in ℤ.
Whole, so also an integer. Not natural.
Natural, so also whole and an integer.

screens.title: Facts about ℤ
items: Decimals and fractions like 2.5 and 3/4 are not integers.
Every natural number is whole. Every whole number is an integer.

points.info: The middle. Neither positive nor negative.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A whole number or the negative of a whole number.
A line with 0 in the middle, positives right and negatives left.

screens.text: Positive integers: true or false? 0 ∈ ℤ⁺
screens.why:
ℤ⁺ is the set of positive integers: {1, 2, 3, …}.
0 is neither positive nor negative.
So 0 is not in ℤ⁺. False.
0 is in ℤ and in 𝕎.

An integer has no fraction or decimal part.
0, 12, −294 and 455 have none, so they are integers.
2 1/3 and 2/5 are fractions. 1.02 and 0.25 are decimals.
So they are not integers.
screens.clue: Does it have a fraction or decimal part?

screens.why:
Negative numbers are to the left of 0.
−2 is 2 steps from 0.
Start at 0 and move 2 steps left: −1, then −2.

screens.ask: Missing mark: on a number line the marks go S, −15, −10, R, 0, 5. Each step is the same. R = ___
screens.why:
Step 1: find one step: from −15 to −10 is 5.
Step 2: check: from 0 to 5 is also 5.
Step 3: R comes one step after −10: −10 + 5 = −5.
Check: one more step from −5 gives 0. ✓
screens.clue: Find the size of one step first.

screens.text: Sets of integers: true or false? ℤ⁺ ∪ ℤ⁻ = ℤ
screens.why:
ℤ⁺ = {1, 2, 3, …} and ℤ⁻ = {−1, −2, −3, …}.
Their union holds every positive and every negative integer.
But 0 is in neither set.
0 ∈ ℤ, so the union is not all of ℤ. False.
screens.clue: Which integer is neither positive nor negative?

screens.text: Sets of integers: which set is ℤ⁺ ∪ {0}?
screens.why:
ℤ⁺ = {1, 2, 3, …}.
Add 0: {0, 1, 2, 3, …}.
That is the set of whole numbers 𝕎.
ℕ has no 0. ℤ also has the negatives.
screens.clue: Write ℤ⁺ and add 0 to it.

en.text: Opposite numbers are the same distance from zero on different sides, like 7 and minus 7. The opposite of a is minus a, and the opposite of minus a is a. The opposite of zero is zero. A gain of 120 birr is the opposite of a loss of 120 birr.

screens.title: Pairs around 0
screens.ask: Tap the points. What do the pairs share?

screens.title: Definition 2.4
paras: Opposite numbers are at the same distance from zero, in opposite directions.
The opposite of zero is zero.

screens.title: Note
paras: For any integer a: the opposite of a is −a.
−(−a) = a. The opposite of a negative number is positive.
The opposite of a positive number is negative.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Two numbers at the same distance from 0 on different sides.

screens.ask: Opposite numbers: the opposite of 70 is ___
screens.why:
The opposite is the same distance from 0, on the other side.
70 is 70 steps right of 0.
So its opposite is 70 steps left: −70.

screens.ask: Opposites on the number line: tap the opposite of −3.
screens.why:
−3 is 3 steps to the left of 0.
The opposite is the same distance on the other side.
So go 3 steps to the right of 0: the opposite is 3.
screens.clue: How far is −3 from 0? Go the same distance the other way.

screens.ask: Opposite numbers: the opposite of −23 is ___
screens.why:
−23 is 23 steps left of 0.
Its opposite is 23 steps right of 0.
So −(−23) = 23.
screens.clue: The opposite of a negative number is positive.

screens.text: Opposite quantities: what is the opposite of a gain of Birr 120?
screens.why:
A gain of Birr 120 is +120.
The opposite has the same size, other sign: −120.
−120 is a loss of Birr 120.
Birr 0 has a different size, so it is not the opposite.

screens.ask: Opposite temperatures: Hawassa is 9 °C above zero. Bale has the opposite temperature. Bale = ___ °C
screens.why:
Hawassa is 9 °C above zero: +9.
The opposite has the same size, other sign.
So Bale is −9 °C (9 °C below zero).

screens.ask: Opposite of an opposite: work out −(−(−5)) = ___
screens.why:
Work from the inside out.
−(−5) is the opposite of −5, which is 5.
Then −(5) is the opposite of 5, which is −5.
Three minus signs give a negative answer: −5.
screens.clue: Take the opposite three times, one at a time.

screens.title: ℕ and 𝕎
steps: So 0 is whole but not natural.

screens.text: Natural and whole numbers: which number is whole but not natural?
screens.why:
Whole numbers: 0, 1, 2, 3, …
Natural numbers: 1, 2, 3, …
0 is in the first list only.
So 0 is whole but not natural.

items.ask: Missing mark: on a number line the marks go A, −7, B, −5, C, … in steps of 1. A = ___
items.why:
Each step is 1.
A is one step to the left of −7.
Left means smaller: −7 − 1 = −8.
So A = −8 (and B = −6, C = −4).

The minus sign in front of a number is read "negative".
So −3 is read "negative three".
"Positive three" is +3.
items.clue: How do we read the − sign?

items.ask: Writing integers: write "negative fifty-three" as a numeral: ___
items.why:
"Negative" means a minus sign.
"Fifty-three" is 53.
So the numeral is −53.

items.ask: Write the change with a sign: a rise of 10 °C is written ___
items.why:
A rise means the temperature goes up.
Going up is positive.
So a rise of 10 °C is +10 (or just 10).

ℤ = {…, −3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, …}.
−2 is in this list.
It is a negative integer. True.
items.clue: Is −2 a whole number or its negative?

items.why:
2.5 has a decimal part: 2.5 = 2 + 0.5.
Integers have no decimal part.
So 2.5 is not in ℤ. False.

items.text: Sets of numbers: true or false? ℕ = ℤ⁺
items.why:
ℕ = {1, 2, 3, …}.
ℤ⁺ = {1, 2, 3, …}, the positive integers.
The two lists are the same. True.

items.text: Sets of numbers: true or false? 𝕎 ∪ ℕ = ℕ
items.why:
𝕎 = {0, 1, 2, …} and ℕ = {1, 2, 3, …}.
The union has every number in either set: {0, 1, 2, …} = 𝕎.
0 is in the union but not in ℕ.
So 𝕎 ∪ ℕ = 𝕎, not ℕ. False.

items.text: Sets of numbers: what is the relationship between whole numbers, natural numbers and integers?
items.why:
Every natural number is a whole number: ℕ ⊂ 𝕎.
Every whole number is an integer: 𝕎 ⊂ ℤ.
So ℕ ⊂ 𝕎 ⊂ ℤ. ℤ is the biggest set.
ℤ ⊂ 𝕎 is wrong: −1 is in ℤ but not in 𝕎.

items.ask: Opposite numbers: the opposite of −170 is ___
items.why:
−170 is 170 steps left of 0.
Its opposite is 170 steps right of 0.
So −(−170) = 170.

items.ask: Opposite numbers: the opposite of 0 is ___
items.why:
0 is at distance 0 from itself.
No step left or right is needed.
So the opposite of 0 is 0.

items.text: Opposite quantities: what is the opposite of 15 °C above zero?
items.why:
15 °C above zero is +15.
The opposite has the same size, other sign: −15.
−15 means 15 °C below zero.

items.text: Opposite quantities: what is the opposite of a walk of 5 km backward?
items.why:
Backward is negative: −5.
The opposite is +5.
+5 means a walk of 5 km forward.

test.ask: Write the temperature with a sign: 5 °C below zero is written ___ °C
test.why:
Below zero means less than 0.
Numbers less than 0 get a minus sign.
So 5 °C below zero is −5 °C.

An integer has no fraction or decimal part.
−7, 0 and 12 are integers.
0.5 is a decimal and 3/4 is a fraction.
So they are not integers.

test.ask: Opposite numbers: the opposite of −48 is ___
test.why:
−48 is 48 steps left of 0.
Its opposite is 48 steps right of 0.
So −(−48) = 48.

test.text: Zero: true or false? Zero is a positive integer.
test.why:
Positive integers are 1, 2, 3, …
Negative integers are −1, −2, −3, …
Zero is in neither list: it is neither positive nor negative.
So the statement is false.

test.text: Sets of numbers: which statement is true?
test.why:
Every whole number 0, 1, 2, … is an integer. So 𝕎 ⊂ ℤ is true.
ℤ ⊂ 𝕎 is false: −1 is an integer but not whole.
ℕ = 𝕎 is false: 0 is whole but not natural.
